Abandoned

Dropping this as a conclusion of a discussion here and on Discord. Another patch, that invalidates LogToLogService action, will be pushed instead.

?  I'm not following this statement;  I didn't see support for logs added to https://github.com/openbmc/telemetry

Is there something I'm missing?
It has been added some time ago: https://github.com/openbmc/telemetry/commit/8018a3ba9782e85ac49686a454183dc4580547e9. Added reference URL to commit message.
That feature doesn't seem to take into account TelemetryService at all?

Triggers are part of TelemetryService schema: https://github.com/openbmc/bmcweb/blob/master/redfish-core/schema/dmtf/csdl/TelemetryService_v1.xml#L199-L204. Its backend implementation supports logging to Redfish log, which has been standarized in a commit mentioned in my previous comment. Is this a valid reason to include a reference to LogService?
Ed, what's your take on this?

My take is that the commit message needs to be updated with WHY we're adding this.  Why is this property useful to a client?  What does it indicate and how does a consumer of it use the property?  Ideally that would be backed with some level of clarification from either the redfish spec or the redfish forums.

On second thought, I made a mistake during implementation. The actual recipient of logs sent by telemetry service is BMC journal (as it was in the original commit). I apologize for unnecessary confusion. 

I've corrected the URI to a right one. I've also reworked the commit message once again, by adding a reference to Redfish spec among other things. Could You please take a look once again, if it's okay now?
Still needs to answer "why".  How is this useful to a client.
Reworked once again and added an explanation why a client would want this. Could You please take a look?

The original patch you're reverting had the journal here, not EventLog.

https://github.com/openbmc/bmcweb/commit/2b3da45876aac57a36d3093379a992d699e7e396#diff-9009408eb4edf9b9f54269157bfef98b6acd39c6ee87e26c7f0d4eccf0b67179L35

please don't label things as reverts that aren't actually reverts.  it takes up maintainer time.

Lets treat this as a new feature addition, and write a commit message where appropriate.  Why is this correct, what client facing things does it enable?
Rewritten commit message
This doesn't seem right.  The journal isnt' structured logging.  Triggers are structured.

I'm not sure I got this. I thought that journal itself has structured form as well? As per description from freedesktop journald documentation, "it creates and maintains structured, indexed journals based on logging information that is received from a variety of sources" (ref.: https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd-journald.service.html). Am I missing something?

The test you need to run is this:
1. Set up a trigger.
2. Cause your system to exceed the trigger threshold
3. Check the log service you've specified for Trigger. TriggerNumericAboveUpperWarning message.

That will indicate which log service your message is going to, and what should be in this property.  Also keep in mind that this log service is dependent on meson options, so please make sure that you add the appropriate meson options.  If journal messageid logging is disabled, this property shouldn't show up.

This is exactly how I've tested it prior to opening the review. I've appended the commit message with exact steps. To sum up, there are 3 possible trigger action values to set up:

- LogToLogService - upon activation, a journal log will be created by Telemetry service (e.g. Discrete condition 'OnChange' of trigger 'TelemetryService/TestTriggerDiscreteOnChange' is met on sensor: /redfish/v1/Chassis/AVC_Baseboard/Sensors/temperature_Right_DIMM_Bank_Temp, recorded value: 24.187000, timestamp: 2025-07-15T10:10:45.505Z), and a corresponding entry will be added to /redfish/v1/Managers/bmc/LogServices/Journal

- RedfishEvent - activation creates an entry in /redfish/v1/Systems/system/LogServices/EventLog/Entries (example entry might contain "MessageId": "Telemetry.1.0.TriggerDiscreteConditionMet")

- RedfishMetricReport - activation will initiate creation of a Report specified by one or more MetricReportDefinition objects listed within `Links` property.

The situation covered by this patch is the first one. Code responsible for creating a journal entry is present here: https://github.com/openbmc/telemetry/blob/7d87668cf590570896bfb33974b06fbdc16bc47b/src/trigger_actions.cpp, LogToJournal::commit. 

If I understand correctly, Your concern is that journal entry doesn't contain message ID pointing to corresponding entry from Redfish Message Registry (such as TriggerNumericAboveUpperWarning or TriggerDiscreteConditionMet)? I guess this can be corrected on backened by adding a proper field to journal entry, or even reshaping the whole message so that it matches the schema.

> Your concern is that journal entry doesn't contain message ID pointing to corresponding entry from Redfish Message Registry 

Correct, that and even if we did contain the correct message id, there isn't mode checks to ensure that we're in the right mode.

My 5 cents:

>I guess this can be corrected on backened by adding a proper field to journal entry, or even reshaping the whole message so that it matches the schema.

Okay, so we don't follow the Data Model. Per `TriggerActionMessage`:
```
Telemetry : Messages from the Telemetry Message Registry.
• This value shall indicate that messages generated in response to a trigger action shall utilize
messages from the Telemetry Message Registry. If this property is not supplied or supported, this
value should be used as the default for this trigger
```

It seems like we've uncovered that implementation on the `openbmc/telemetry` side is lacking. It seems that this property and description was added after `Trigger` schema was implemented, which would explain the discrepancy. To make the implementation proper, we should bump schema to 1.4+ and revisit all journal logs.

For instance:
https://github.com/openbmc/telemetry/blob/7d87668cf590570896bfb33974b06fbdc16bc47b/src/trigger_actions.cpp#L176 should be rather defined and expressed like TriggerDiscreteConditionMet mandates.

I'm still not clear what the expected format in `LogService` should be. Is it fair to assume that Journal entry, currently like this:
```
{
  "@odata.id": "/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc/LogServices/Journal/Entries/ad02a87606fb4cec92f34f5be3e33301_1617606480490",
  "@odata.type": "#LogEntry.v1_9_0.LogEntry",
  "Created": "2025-07-17T10:13:39.344178+00:00",
  "EntryType": "Oem",
  "Id": "ad02a87606fb4cec92f34f5be3e33301_1617606480490",
  "Message": "rsyslogd: imjournal: journal files changed, reloading... [v8.2402.0 try https://www.rsyslog.com/e/0 ]",
  "Name": "BMC Journal Entry",
  "OemRecordFormat": "BMC Journal Entry",
  "Severity": "OK"
}
```

should be replaced with properly formatted `Redfish Event`, as expressed by `redfish/v1/Systems/system/LogServices/EventLog/Entries`, eg:
```
{
  "@odata.id": "/redfish/v1/Systems/system/LogServices/EventLog/Entries/1749736186",
  "@odata.type": "#LogEntry.v1_9_0.LogEntry",
  "Created": "2025-06-12T13:49:46+00:00",
  "EntryType": "Event",
  "Id": "1749736186",
  "Message": "Invalid username or password attempted on HTTPS.",
  "MessageArgs": [
    "HTTPS"
  ],
  "MessageId": "OpenBMC.0.1.InvalidLoginAttempted",
  "Name": "System Event Log Entry",
  "Severity": "Warning"
}
```
?

If so - what's the point of having separate implementation? Perhaps what we need to do under the hood is to treat `LogToLogService`  equivalently to `RedfishEvent` , just have extra property to point user to the `redfish/v1/Systems/system/LogServices/EventLog`?

> Also keep in mind that this log service is dependent on meson options, so please make sure that you add the appropriate meson options. If journal messageid logging is disabled, this property shouldn't show up.

I assume that `redfish-bmc-journal` is the option You had in mind. Did a minor change in code. Could You take a look and specify whether it's a step in the right direction?

The code can answer it better than I can.  If the above behavior doesn't work with the option, then it needs fixed.

> If so - what's the point of having separate implementation?

Some people didn't like the implementation that was there.

Journal gives raw access to the journal.  EventLog gives structured access over dbus (which is also in the journal).

> It seems like we've reached our goal of having implementation consistent with intent of the spec (at least on the Properties side).

I don't see that to be the case, and if we had done that, we need some level of tested statement that shows that we are generating the appropriate message, otherwise we haven't met the intent of the spec.
Still doesn't answer WHY a client would want this.

**Ed**
>>If so - what's the point of having separate implementation?
>
> Some people didn't like the implementation that was there.

> Journal gives raw access to the journal. EventLog gives structured access over dbus (which is also in the journal).

I get that Journal and EventLog are not the same. 

Given the assumptions that:
* Trigger message should adhere to `Telemetry Message Registry`;
* We have `TriggerAction` which does that, through emitting an `RedfishEvent`, stored in `EventLog`;

We have following options:
**Option 1: Make Journal spec-compliant**

1) Re-work `openmbc/telemetry` backend side to emit properly formatted events

Probably would need to adjust the `Journal/Entries` implementation so that if `Redfish Event`-like-message is spotted, event exposed on the Redfish is properly formatted. In other words - for `Trigger` logs you should see `Entries` formatted like they were directly ripped from `EventLog`.

**Option 2: Invalidate `LogToLogService`**
If we need extra effort just to make the same events appear in different place in the tree, what would be the point? We need to know answers to following question:
What's the use case? Why would anyone want to have the same Events stored in the `Journal` while he could use `RedfishEvent` instead? 

The only differences I could think of are:
* user wouldn't like the logs to persist across BMC reboots (this is probably implementation specific)
* user wouldn't like this log to be emitted (`Redfish Event` vs `Message` semantics)

I'd argue, that if we don't have arguments against **Option 2** we should save us the effort and go with it.
